description.value: The study examined neurocognitive and neuroanatomic correlates of letter and semantic verbal fluency deficits across frontotemporal lobar degeneration subgroups using neuropsychological testing and MRI voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: In the current research, FTLD patients diagnosed with bvFTLD, SemD, and PNFA were compared on letter (FAS) and semantic verbal fluency tests.

value: We hypothesized that letter and semantic fluency measures depend on partially overlapping large-scale neural networks that support search and retrieval mechanisms in the mental lexicon and that partially distributed patterns of impairment would be evident in each FTLD subgroup.

spans.text: structured clinical interview

description.value: Structured clinical interview used as part of the consensus diagnostic process for frontotemporal lobar degeneration subgroups.

Patients completed letter fluency and semantic fluency tests. Letter fluency required generating words beginning with each of the letters F, A, and S for 60 seconds per letter. Semantic fluency required producing as many animal names as possible in 60 seconds.

instructions.value: For letter fluency, generate words beginning with a specified letter, excluding proper nouns, numbers, and multiple forms of the same word. For semantic fluency, produce as many names of animals as possible, excluding perseverations and extracategory intrusions.

value: Number of correct letter-fluency responses summed across F, A, and S
